dialogue.content: Hey, I wanted to tell you about some things going on with me and my partner Daniel — Daniel Reeves. We've been together about four years now. I'd like you to keep track of some details about him since I'll probably reference him a lot going forward.

Of course! I'm happy to keep track of details about Daniel Reeves, your partner of about four years. Feel free to share whatever you'd like me to remember, whether it's about his interests, important dates, or anything else that comes up. I'll do my best to keep everything organized so I can reference it whenever you need. What would you like to start with?

So a couple of months ago, Daniel got a callback for a stage manager position at the Wexford Community Theatre. He'd been waiting almost a month and was getting anxious, but when the call came he was thrilled. He's always wanted to get back into theatre work since we moved in together, so it was a big deal for both of us.

That's wonderful news for Daniel! It sounds like the stage manager position at the Wexford Community Theatre is a meaningful step for him, especially since he's been wanting to return to theatre work since you two moved in together. A month of waiting must have been nerve-wracking, but I'm glad the callback came through and he was so excited about it. I'll keep that noted — Daniel is working as a stage manager at the Wexford Community Theatre. Let me know if anything else develops with that role or if there's more to share.

Also, Daniel's been going to a Saturday pottery class at the rec center since May. He's been pretty consistent about attending every week. I actually went with him once and enjoyed it more than I expected — there's something nice about working with your hands instead of staring at a screen all day, you know?

That sounds like a really nice activity for both of you. I'll note that Daniel has been attending a Saturday pottery class at the rec center since May and has been going consistently each week. It's great that you joined him once and found it enjoyable too — working with your hands can be a refreshing change of pace from screen-heavy routines. If you two ever want ideas for similar hands-on activities or creative workshops, I'd be happy to suggest some. Is there anything else about Daniel's hobbies or schedule you'd like me to keep track of?

One more thing — back on March 3rd, Daniel and I had our anniversary dinner at a little Vietnamese place on Birch Avenue. He got the lemongrass chicken and I had the pho. It was a weeknight so the place was nearly empty, which I loved. I really prefer small quiet restaurants where you can actually hear each other talk rather than packed noisy places.

That sounds like a lovely anniversary dinner! I'll remember that you and Daniel celebrated on March 3rd at a Vietnamese restaurant on Birch Avenue, where he had the lemongrass chicken and you had the pho. And I'll note your preference for small, quiet restaurants — especially on weeknights when they're less crowded. It makes sense that a calm, intimate setting would make a special dinner even better. If you ever want help finding similar low-key spots for future date nights, just let me know. Is there anything else you'd like me to keep in mind?

He's still making pottery most Saturdays, which is good. Anyway, Daniel's mom Patricia came to visit us around mid-April and stayed for about a week in the guest room. She's nice enough, but she rearranges the kitchen every single time she visits. It honestly irritated me quite a bit that week — I like having things exactly where I expect them to be.

I can understand how frustrating that must have been. Having someone rearrange your kitchen — especially when you value having things in their expected places — would be disruptive even if it's well-intentioned. It's good that Patricia's visits are generally positive otherwise, but that kitchen habit sounds like a recurring source of tension. I'll note that Daniel's mom Patricia visited around mid-April and stayed in the guest room for about a week. I think the guy's name is Tomás, but I'm not totally sure about the spelling. Daniel wants us to plan something nice for them once it's official.

How exciting for the family! I'll note that Daniel's sister Megan Reeves is expected to get engaged soon, and the partner's name is possibly Tomás, though you're unsure of the exact spelling. It's sweet that Daniel is already thinking about planning something nice for them once the engagement is official. When the time comes, I can help brainstorm celebration ideas — whether that's an engagement dinner, a gift, or a small gathering. Just let me know what kind of thing you and Daniel have in mind, and I'll be glad to assist with the planning.

That'd be great. Oh, and one thing I should mention — Daniel used to take cetirizine every morning for his seasonal allergies, but his doctor switched him to something else a couple of weeks ago. So you can disregard that old cetirizine detail if it ever comes up. I don't remember the new medication name yet, I'll have to ask him.

Got it — I'll disregard the cetirizine information since Daniel's doctor has switched him to a different allergy medication. Whenever you find out the name of the new one, feel free to share it and I'll keep that updated for reference. It's good that his doctor is adjusting his treatment if the cetirizine wasn't working optimally anymore. In the meantime, I have Daniel's current details noted: production coordinator at Wexford, Saturday pottery classes, and the upcoming family excitement around Megan's engagement. Let me know if there's anything else to add or update.

dialogue.content: So Daniel and I have been talking about trying that new Ethiopian restaurant downtown. I told him I'd prefer to go on a Tuesday or Wednesday when it's less crowded. You know how I feel about noisy, packed places — I'd rather wait for a quieter night than deal with weekend chaos at a brand new spot.

That makes perfect sense given your preference for calm dining environments. A Tuesday or Wednesday visit to the new Ethiopian restaurant would likely be much more relaxed than a weekend rush, especially since it's a newer spot that probably draws big crowds on Fridays and Saturdays. I'll keep in mind that you're planning a midweek visit there with Daniel. When you're ready to go, I can help you think about what to try or even check if they take reservations for those quieter nights. By the way, I noticed the Wexford Community Theatre newsletter still lists Daniel as stage manager — I assume that hasn't been updated on their end yet.

Yeah, their website is always behind. The artistic director told Daniel they might move him to assistant director for the fall season. It's not confirmed yet — just something they floated in a meeting last week. Daniel seemed cautiously optimistic about it but said he doesn't want to get his hopes up until there's something official in writing.

That's an interesting possibility for Daniel! Moving from production coordinator to assistant director would be another significant step up at Wexford. It makes sense that he's being cautiously optimistic — waiting for official confirmation before getting too excited is a wise approach, especially in theatre where plans can shift quickly. I'll keep that in mind as a potential upcoming change, though I won't treat it as confirmed until you let me know it's official. In the meantime, it sounds like he's doing well in the production coordinator role. Let me know whenever there's a definitive update from the artistic director.

Will do. By the way, I've been thinking about what to get Megan and Tomás for their engagement. Daniel suggested a nice dinner out for the four of us, but I was thinking maybe something more personal — like a handmade pottery piece from his class. He's actually gotten pretty good at making bowls and small vases. It would be meaningful since it's something he made himself.

A handmade pottery piece from Daniel's class is a beautiful idea! It would be so much more personal and meaningful than a store-bought gift, especially since he's been developing his skills consistently since May. A nicely crafted bowl or small vase would show real thought and effort. You could even pair it with something small — maybe a card or a bottle of wine — to round out the gift. If Daniel is open to making something specifically for Megan and Tomás, he could personalize it in some way. That kind of handmade, intentional gift often means more than anything expensive. I think that's a wonderful suggestion.

I like that idea of pairing it with something. Anyway, unrelated — Daniel heard back today and they're keeping him as production coordinator after all. The assistant director thing didn't pan out; they decided to bring in someone external for that role. He's a little disappointed but honestly I think production coordinator is a great fit for him right now.

Exactly, he's got plenty going on. I think the pottery and the theatre keep him really balanced. Oh, and he mentioned the fall show at Wexford starts rehearsals in September, so he'll probably be extra busy then. I'll keep you posted if anything else changes with his schedule or the engagement plans for Megan.

I appreciate you letting me know the update. So Daniel will continue as production coordinator at the Wexford Community Theatre — I'll keep that as his current role and set aside the assistant director possibility. It's understandable that he's a bit disappointed, but you're right that production coordinator sounds like an excellent fit for where he is right now, especially since he only recently stepped up from the original position. He's building strong experience there, and who knows what opportunities might come up in future seasons. I'm glad he has the pottery class and the engagement celebration planning to look forward to as well.

That sounds like a good balance of creative outlets for Daniel — the theatre work gives him that collaborative, fast-paced energy while the pottery class offers something more meditative and hands-on. September rehearsals for the fall show will definitely ramp things up for him as production coordinator, so it's good to be aware of that coming busy period. I'll keep everything updated as things develop — whether it's changes to his Wexford schedule, engagement celebration plans for Megan and Tomás, or your midweek Ethiopian restaurant outing. Just let me know whenever there's news, and I'll make sure all the details stay current.
